title: The Baby Monitor
intro: Some voices carry further than they should. The lantern is lit.
body: My daughter Lily is four. She sleeps with the baby monitor on. Last night, at twelve past three, it crackled. Lily was whispering. "I can't. Mummy will hear." Then another voice. Low. Patient. "Mummy is asleep." I ran. Her door was shut. Her night-light was off. I had left it on. Lily was asleep, facing the wall. Nobody else. I sat on her floor until dawn, the monitor in my lap. At twenty to five, it crackled again. Lily hadn't moved. Then the voice came, so close it touched the microphone. "Mummy's awake now."
outro: Lily is five now. She still won't sleep without the monitor. She says he likes to listen.

At twenty to five, it crackled again. Lily hadn't moved. Then the voice came, so close it touched the microphone. "Mummy's awake now."
